test_title: RRB Technician Grade 1 20 Dec 2024 Shift 1 Official Paper
subject: general
question: In a survey of 260 students in a school, 100 were listed as taking apple juice, 150 as taking orange juice and 75 were listed as taking both apple as well as orange juice. Find how many students were taking neither apple juice nor orange juice.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total students (n(U)) = 260

At least one juice = n(Apple) + n(Orange) − n(Both) = 100 + 150 − 75 = 175

Neither juice = Total students − At least one juice = 260 − 175 = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students surveyed = 260

Students taking **Apple juice** (n(A)) = 100

Students taking **Orange juice** (n(O)) = 150

Students taking **Both juices** (n(A ∩ O)) = 75

**Formula Used:**

n(A ∪ O) = n(A) + n(O) − n(A ∩ O)

Students taking neither = Total − n(A ∪ O)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42cbb40842faa8181b348ec211591d5b0ad6968e9e9fa5f4c1c9ab57dc5210d6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Students taking at least one juice = 100 + 150 − 75

⇒ n(A ∪ O) = 175

⇒ Students taking neither juice = 260 − 175

⇒ Result = 85

**∴ The correct answer is 85 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Venn Diagram Basics

A Venn diagram represents sets as circles within a rectangle (Universal set). The overlap represents the intersection (A ∩ B).

De Morgan's Laws

The number of elements in neither set is denoted by (A ∪ B)' which is equal to n(U) − n(A ∪ B).

Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion

For three sets: n(A∪B∪C) = n(A)+n(B)+n(C) − n(A∩B) − n(B∩C) − n(C∩A) + n(A∩B∩C).</p
